 Jamey Eisenberg's Week 8 Fantasy football sleepers and DFS picks: Makai Lemon could be a bitter sweet surprise
 With injuries opening doors across the NFL, Jamey Eisenberg highlights Makai Lemon and other sleepers who could deliver big
 By
 Jamey Eisenberg 
 Oct 30, 2026
 at
 6:25 pm ET 
 •
 4 min read
 Imagn Images Imagn Images 
 Emeka Egbuka (foot) was ruled out for Week 8, and A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Carnell Tate (shoulder) are not expected to play. That opens the door for several sleepers on the Buccaneers , Patriots and Titans . 
In Tampa Bay, Chris Godwin should be viewed as a No. 3 Fantasy receiver against Atlanta; Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson are each worth a flier in deeper leagues and Cade Otton is a streaming tight end. Egbuka didn't play in Week 7 at Carolina, but the Buccaneers only attempted 11 passes, with the run game and defense dominating the Panthers . 
That might not happen against the Falcons , who are No. 11 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing receivers. Godwin had five targets against Carolina and finished with four catches for 27 yards. He has yet to score a touchdown or reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, but he has scored at least 10.3 PPR points in four games in a row against Atlanta. 
Hurst has two games this season with at least six targets, and he scored 11 PPR points in one of them. And Johnson caught his first touchdown of the season in Week 7 with Egbuka out but only had two catches for 33 yards. Of that duo, I would lean toward Hurst, but either one could be viable against the Falcons. 
Atlanta is No. 9 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing tight ends, and Otton scored at least 8.6 PPR points in two of four outings with Baker Mayfield this year. All of these guys should be in play for Mayfield with Egbuka out. 
For New England, Hunter Henry is my favorite pass catcher, and I like him as a top-five Fantasy tight end in all leagues. He has scored at least 11.2 PPR points in four games in a row, including two touchdowns over that span, and the Dolphins are No. 3 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing tight ends. Eli Raridon , who has scored at least 10.7 PPR points in two of his past three games, is also worth a look as a streamer in deeper leagues. 
At receiver, Demario Douglas struggled in Week 7 at Chicago with three catches for 23 yards on four targets, but he scored at least 19.6 PPR points in each of his previous two games against Las Vegas and the Jets . I like Douglas as a high-end No. 3 receiver in all leagues. 
 Efton Chism III scored at least 10.9 PPR points in the two games before Brown returned from his ankle injury in Week 6. He had 10 targets over that span and finished with seven catches for 99 yards and a touchdown, and Chism is worth a flier in deeper leagues. Just keep in mind that Miami is No. 3 in fewest Fantasy points allowed to opposing receivers, and this should be a great game for Rhamondre Stevenson . 
In Tennessee, the only pass catcher I would consider starting in three-receiver leagues is Wan'Dale Robinson at Cincinnati. He has struggled in his past two games against Indianapolis and Cleveland with seven catches for 29 yards and no touchdowns on 13 targets, but he scored at least 11 PPR points in each of his three games prior to that against the Giants , Ravens and Texans . 
The Bengals have allowed three receivers in their past two games to score at least 12 PPR points, and Robinson should lead the Titans in targets with Tate out.
